summary: Executed the determinism and seed suite on a 20,000-row linked subset. Two independent seed-42 runs produced byte-identical files for all ten outputs, and an approximately 63,000-check comparison found no failure. With seed 43, every seeded business-reference value changed (every applicable row), every fake email and phone value changed, and every noise value changed; hash, mask, and redact columns had zero seed differences and matched their policy formulas. Parsed fake dates shifted by 1 to 3650 days, satisfying the minimum offset, and Gaussian deltas had means near zero with standard deviations of about 0.98-1.02 for sigma=1 fields and 9.61-10.22 for sigma=10 fields. A full ten-file same-seed repeat was started but an environment restart killed it after two outputs; the completed first file was byte-identical and the truncated second file matched the baseline byte-for-byte up to its about 295,000th row. This supports deterministic, seed-responsive behavior but leaves the complete second full run unfinished. Evidence strength is a linked-subset experiment plus a partial full-data prefix; no official verifier was run.
next_hint: Determinism and seed behavior are supported. The next question is whether the observed cross-file equality is actually caused by the union edges or is partly an artifact of exact-string normalization.
